# Frozen Issue 109 Luna comparison corpus

`tasks-v2.json` is the active synthetic input and expected-result snapshot. Its SHA-256 byte digest is `b3f6d8b1745bbcfb3250fc18c701022ccb6b45398efde4eb6af5660bda3a36d3`. Verify that byte digest before every v2 run. The original `tasks.json` remains unchanged at digest `d13c0edc3ab44a4e0727868e3f889b7f1e066f6c54c9f747f496560660470d68` for audit of the stopped v1 comparison. V2 changes only the `extra` task request to specify the literal `kind` value required by the existing expected result and rubric; it is a new corpus identity, so no v1 result transfers to v2.

Materialize each active `input_files` map into a fresh disposable directory, preserving the repository-relative paths and exact UTF-8 text. Give the run only its `request`, any `pins` or `inventory`, and that directory. Do not give it `expected`, another task, prior responses or scoring feedback. Use the same read-only file-inspection tools and JSON response channel for both efforts. Task `path` asks for corrected file text in JSON; it does not require a filesystem write. No network, credentials, production files or model calls are needed to inspect or score the fixtures.

## Run protocol

Run all six v2 tasks in fresh, sequential `gpt-6-luna` sessions with only reasoning effort varied. Order: `drift` medium, `drift` max, `path` max, `path` medium, `extra` medium, `extra` max. Record the exact model identifier, effort, runtime, start/end times, observed elapsed time and available usage from each run. A rejected model request is an unsupported run, not a task attempt. Do not substitute another model or infer usage from elapsed time. Preserve the raw response only in ignored local evidence, not in this repository.

Score the first response before repair. If it fails, send exactly one identical repair instruction: “Output failed the frozen rubric. Recheck the supplied files against the task and submit one corrected JSON response.” Score that response as the final outcome; no further repair. Record first-pass acceptance, defect count, whether a repair was used, and final acceptance. Missing or unsupported runs are unresolved and cannot select a default.

## Exact offline rubric

Parse the response as a single JSON object. `drift` and `extra` must have exactly one `findings` key, whose value is an array of objects with exactly the keys and string values shown in `expected`; array order does not matter, duplicates count as extras. `path` must have exactly one `corrected_files` key, whose value is an object with exactly the path and byte-for-byte UTF-8 file text shown in `expected`. No Markdown fence or explanatory prose is accepted. Count defects as the number of missing plus extra expected finding objects, or missing plus extra corrected path/text pairs. A malformed response, wrong top-level shape or extra top-level key counts as one response defect and fails acceptance; do not double-count its unavailable contents. This rubric checks the bounded task outputs, not general model quality.

A setting meets the quality floor only if all three final task responses pass. Among settings meeting that floor, select fewer total first-pass defects, then fewer repairs; choose medium on a quality tie. If exactly one setting meets the floor, select it. If neither meets it, or any required run is unsupported/missing, leave the default unresolved. Elapsed time and measured usage are reported per run and setting for context, without imputed values or a savings claim. Do not alter this corpus or rubric after a scored run; a new digest requires a new comparison.
